correctness.rationale: The exact candidate-facet conditioned spherical density is proportional to (1−h²)^((d²−2d−1)/2)F_d(h)^m, including signed h, m=n−d. The negative log-density in y=dh has V≥κ_d=1−2/d−1/d²>0 for d≥3, giving the finite-sample centered sub-Gaussian bound. With rho=m/d→finite, a uniform local Gaussian expansion gives moving saddle r_rho defined by r=rho φ(r)/Φ(r) and variance [1+rho λ(r)(r+λ(r))]^(−1). Strong convexity supplies tails so local Laplace expansion upgrades to total variation and moments. The Gaussian-model facet offset has tilted N(0,1/d) density and same saddle; TV comparison follows. Taylor r_rho=μrho−μ³rho²+O(rho³) yields the precise m~d^(3/4) linear-centering transition. Independently solved five saddle equations rho=0,.1,.5,1,3, obtained variances 1,.941626,.779898,.661296,.461297 and checked positivity and monotonicity. The finite calculations corroborate, not prove, the Laplace theorem.
